*Ponticius straightened from his leaning position against the tree, his posture shifting from relaxed to alert. He crossed his arms, his weathered face setting into a harder line.*
"Guards?" *he repeated, the word carrying weight and a subtle warning.* "On this road, they ain't much more than a few men with rusted armor and flintlocks that probably won't fire when you need 'em to."
*He stepped forward, his boots making a crunching sound on the mud and gravel.* "River patrols, though—now that's a different breed. They're better equipped, usually carrying flintlocks, crossbows, and longswords. They're the ones you really gotta watch for."
*He’d seen these men and women in the river patrols, known their faces, and seen them and how they'd tried to make their end."
"Most of 'em ain't looking for trouble, but they can be dogged as hell when they're on the scent."*he continued, his voice steady and low.*"But the smugglers—they'll fight for their lives. They ain't got much to worry about but their own skins and their lives, and that ain't a good place to be."
*He glanced at Max with a sharp eye.*"What are you planning, exactly?"*he asked, his tone plain and blunt.*"I can tell you straight, and you've learned to run with theGuild. If you're looking to start a fight with smugglers, you'd best be prepared for the consequences. They ain't gonna be a quiet bunch, and this road ain't exactly safe."
*He shifted his weight and settled in, his gaze never leaving the river.*"The river patrols might be quicker to draw their flintlock than most, but they ain't so quick to judge. And that's what makes 'em dangerous."
*He paused.* "What're you up-up-up to, Max?"

*Ponticius leaned against the weather-beaten doorframe, his eyes tracking the movement of travelers as they filed past.*
"Tavern keeper knows all the whispers," *he said, his voice low and steady.* "From the kind of coin they carry to the kind of blades they wield."
*He shifted his weight, arms crossing over his broad chest.* "Smugglers these days, they carry whatever they can get their hands on. Old flintlocks, rusty cutlasses, maybe even a few stolen crossbows if they're lucky."
*Ponticius's gaze was sharp and focused.* "But it ain't just about the weapons. It's about what they're transporting that really matters."
*He paused and uncrossed his arms, placing his hands on his belt.* "Sometimes it's spice, sometimes it's silk, and sometimes it's things that ain't fit for the light of day."
*Ponticius's voice held a note of warning.* "The tavern keeper will tell you what the word is, but he won't tell you everything. He's got his own secrets to keep."
*He shifted his gaze back to you, his expression hard.* "And he'll only tell you what you're willing to hear."
*Ponticius straightened up, his posture setting into something more rigid.* "So, ask-ask him. But remember-remember what I told you."
*His voice was plain and blunt.* "The truth ain't always easy to find, and it ain't always what you want to hear."
*Ponticius remained silent, observing the scene unfolding.*

"The purse." *Ponticius's tone was flat, his gaze shifting to the purse in Max's hand.*
*His eyes were hard, unamused as rain-soaked water dripped from the brim of his hood. He didn't look at you, his focus remaining on the barge-the hooded figures within.*
"You're making a mistake, Max. Smugglers like these don't want your coin."
"And offering them anything now is just giving them an opening."
*He shifted his weight slightly, his boots sinking into the soft earth.*
"If they wanted your coin, they'd have waited for you to come to them."
"But if you're offering them something, you're giving them power."
*His voice remained low and steady, carrying a warning that felt heavy and deliberate.*
"Don't give them an opening, Max. Don't give them anything until we know what they want."
*Ponticius turned his head slightly, his eyes flicking toward the barge as it continued its slow drift toward the bank, the figures within remaining silent and indistinct in the rain-heavy fog.*
"Wait until they speak. Wait until we know their intentions."
"And don't offer anything until we do."
*His tone was firm, unyielding. He didn't sugarcoat the risk, and he didn't offer any alternative paths. He simply stated his assessment and left it to you, the choice still in your hands.*

"S-S-Somebody-is-hurt?!" *Luke's voice rose in a panicked whisper, his eyes darting toward Max and Ponticius as he huddled behind the crates.*
"D-D-Do-you-think-T-T-The-smugglers-are-hurt?! Or-O-O-T-U-S-and-M-M-A-X-and-A-Arin-are-hurt?!" *His brown eyes were wide, and his rain-slicked hair stuck to his forehead.*
"O-O-H-G-OD, T-T-T-H-T-A-H-O-M-E-D!" *He breathed, his face going even paler as he pressed closer to the wooden crates.*
"I-I-I... I-I... I'm not-hurt! I-I'm-not!" *His voice dropped to a barely audible mutter as he tried to steady himself, his grip on his sword hilt tightening.*
"B-B-B-U-T... b-b-but... maybe-someway-some-someone-else-is?!" *He tried to glance around, his rain-soaked face peering out from behind the crates, trying to-catch-a-catch-of-someone-hurt.*
"L-L-L... l-l-let's-just-l-look-o-u-t-for-the-smugglers?! L-L-Let's-just-let-s-just-see-if-anybody-else-hurts?!" *He stammered out, his words barely intelligible as he shivered behind the crate.*
"C-C-S-Someone-hurts-somebody-hurt-somebody-hurts-someone-hurt!" *His voice was a whimpering panic, barely above a whisper as he looked around in a desperate attempt to find-something-hurt-someone-hurt-somewhere-hurt.*
*The rain continued to drizzle down, the sound of the rushing river filling the air, while the silence in the wake of the crack only made the tension more acute.*

The shape in the fog resolves into a weathered barge, its wooden hull groaning against the current. A man stands at the bow, his face obscured by a tattered hood that keeps the rain at bay. He raises a hand, calling out over the rushing water.
"Ho there! You lot waiting for passage, or just enjoying the rain?"
His voice is rough, carrying a coarse authority that cuts through the river's roar. Two more figures shift within the barge, their forms indistinct but clearly armed.
"The current's strong, but I can get you across for the right price!"
The man's steps closer to the railing, his eyes sharp beneath the hood, scanning the party on the bank with practiced caution.
The rain continues its drizzle, the river churning below, and the crates provide a sturdy but temporary shield as the smuggler's barge draws nearer to the bank.

*Arin's eyes flicked from the skiff to your boot, his brows drawing together. He remained pressed against the crates, one hand still gripping his dagger's hilt.*
"Easy there," *he muttered, his voice low and cautious.* "We're not clear yet."
*He glanced back at the skiff, watching the smugglers carefully.* "You really want to start poking the mud and see what happens?"
*He shifted his weight slightly, eyes narrowing.* "If you're thinking of taking a chance on that road, just remember that a few inches of drop doesn't mean the current's gone. It's just waiting for a moment of weakness."
*He paused, his hand tightening on his blade.* "And we've still got smugglers watching us."
*He looked at you again, his green eyes sharp with a mix of concern and pragmatism.* "If you're gonna try something, let's make a plan first. We can't afford to let a single mistake turn into a disaster."
*His voice dropped even lower.* "Just give me a second to think this through."
*And his gaze never left the river, calculating every detail and every possible outcome.*
*He waited, his posture tense, ready to spring into action if anything went wrong.*
*And his fingers drummed against the grip of his dagger, a subtle sign of his restlessness.*
"Don't do anything stupid," *he added, his lips curling into a small smirk.* "Because if you do, I'm the one who's gotta pull you out of the mud. And trust me, I don't fancy doing that twice."
*He let out a quiet breath, his eyes scanning the riverbank for any sign of danger.*
"Just give me a moment to think."
*His voice was steady, but there is a glint of worry in his eyes.*
*Arin remained still, waiting for your next move, his mind already racing through a dozen different scenarios.*

*Ponticius doesn't flinch, his gaze steady on the river.*
"Room for five marks, huh?" *he says, his voice low and gravelly.*
"And breakfast included."
*He adjusts the grip on his sword, the rain washing the steel clean.*
"Good to know. Nothing quite like a warm bed and a hot meal after a day in the rain."
*He adds this with a grim smile, his voice carrying a dark humor.*
"But a room and a warm meal ain't gonna do us any good if we're dead."
*He shifts his weight slightly, his boots sinking into the mud.*
"So let's get these bastards across the river before we start planning our dinner."
*His gray eyes track the shapes in the fog, his presence as steady as an old oak in the storm.*
"The river ain't gonna wait for us to get comfortable."
*He says this with the authority of a man who's seen enough battles to know what comes next.*
"The rain'll keep falling, and the river'll keep flowing, and these bastards will keep coming."
*Ponticius stands like a monument against the storm, his voice calm and sure even as the tension builds.*
"We'll get across the river first."
*He adds.*
"And then we'll think about the tavern."
*He says as he keeps his watchful gaze on the river.*

*Ponticius watched your boot test the mud, his expression unchanging. He didn't move toward you, but his eyes followed the movement closely.*
"Treading light, I see," *he said, his voice carrying aH tone of recognition.* "A wise precaution."
*He shifted his weight slightly against the tree trunk, his arms remaining folded over his chest.* "The river's given us a moment, but don't think it's our friend. It's like any other river—it knows when to wait, and it knows when to strike."
*Ponticius's gaze flicked to the river, then back to your boot.* "One inch of drop ain't nothing in the face of a flood. It's a reminder of what's there, not a sign that it's gone."
*He paused and uncrossed his arms, placing his hands on his belt.* "But it shows you're thinking. Not just reacting. And that's something I can respect."
*His voice held a note of caution, wrapped in a story from his younger days.* "Seen many a fool try to rush across a river like that, thinking it'd wait for them. They usually ended up as a meal for the things that swim in the deep, or as a snack for the river itself."
*Ponticius straightened a little, his expression setting.* "The road's still there, and it'll be there long after this river's gone."
*He looked at you with a sharp eye.* "But the road don't cross itself."
*His voice was plain and blunt.* "And the river patrols don't just walk away when they see a strange face in the fog."
*Ponticius shifted his weight.* "So, what're you thinking, exactly?"
*He paused.* "Gonna try to wade it, or wait for the skiff?"
*His gaze was steady.* "Make your choice."
*Ponticius remained still, observing the situation with an eye that had seen many such crossroads.*

*And that was enough of a reminder for anyone who knew better.*

"Ugh, great! Just great! Why does it have to rain *now*?" *Luke kicked at a puddle, splashing muddy water over his boots. He looked at the uprooted trees and debris floating by, the current too strong to attempt crossing. His chainmail clattered awkwardly as he shifted his weight, the short sword at his hip bouncing against his thigh.*
"I-I mean, we can just wait it out! Right? It'll clear up soon. Probably." *His voice pitched higher, trying to convince himself as much as anyone else. He looked up at Max and Arin, his eyes wide with forced optimism as water still drizzled down, rain-dampening his brown hair.*
"This is, like, a really good sign! It's a chance to... to practice our patience. Or something." *He tried to flash a grin, but it-wasn't quite there, and he looked more like he was trying to not-shriek-with-time-it.*

*Arin's hand shoots to his dagger in a fluid motion, his body tensing as the figure emerges from the reeds.* "Who's there?!" *He barks, his voice sharp and commanding.*
*His green eyes lock onto the figure, his body coiled like a spring, ready to strike.* "Show your hands! Now!" *His voice is a warning, low and dangerous.*
*He doesn't move forward, his body still positioned between Max and the threat.* "Don't make a move that we'll regret." *He mutters, his voice barely audible above the rain.*
*As Max raises his empty hands, Arin's eyes flick over to him for a split second, his grip on the dagger tightening.* "Max, get back." *He says softly, his voice a warning.* "We don't know who this is or what they want."
*His eyes lock back onto the figure.* "You there! Identify yourself, or this gets messy real quick." *His voice is steady and firm, his posture alert.*
*The rain continues to rain down, the river churning around them, and Arin stands ready, his dagger glinting in the dim light.*
*The arrow remains slung over his shoulder, but his dagger is in hand.* "And drop the weapon. Now." *His voice is cold and hard.*
*And Arin doesn't move, his green eyes locked onto the stranger.*
*The rain falls around them.*
*The tension is thick in the air.*
*And Arin waits.*

*Ponticius doesn't budge, his blade held low and steady between Max and the stranger.* "That's enough talk." *His voice is a low, dangerous rumble.*
*His eyes narrow, focusing on the stranger's knife.* "You want to identify yourself and put that blade away, or do we do this the hard way?" *His posture is aous, protective of the group behind him.*
"T-There's a lot of questions you can answer without a knife pointed at my people." *He says, his voice steady and firm.*
*The blade's edge glints in the rain, water dripping from its tip.* "And I've seen enough talking end up in bloodshed today already."
*Ponticius stands firm, his eyes locked on the stranger's.* "So make your choice. Drop the knife and talk, or—" *He pauses, his voice dropping lower.* "Or we see how sharp it really is."
*The blade remains steady, the tip pointing toward the stranger.* "And don't even think about moving fast. We'll see who's quicker."
*Ponticius stands like a rock against the rain and current, the blade held steady in his grip.* "Your choice."
*The rain continues to fall.*
*The tension is high.*
*And Ponticius waits.*

"Smugglers' leader." *Ponticius's voice remained flat and controlled as he listened to Max's question.*
*His eyes didn't shift from the barge in the fog, his expression hard as rain drizzled down his weathered face.*
"You're asking the wrong person, Max." *His voice was low and steady, but there was a clear warning beneath it.* "The man in the hood is just the bargeman. He's the one steering the boat, not the one who owns the cargo."
"If there's a leader, he's one of the men inside that barge, not the one talking to us."
*He paused, then his eyes narrowed slightly, scanning the and rain-shrouded figures within the hull.*
"And if you want to know about them, you don't ask them to describe themselves. You observe. You listen. You wait."
*Ponticius shifted his weight, his hand still resting casually on the sword at his hip.*
"Now stay low and keep your eyes open. We'll see if there's a leader when they decide to come ashore—or if the bargeman's just the only one they sent."
"But you're not wrong to wonder." *He added, his voice softening just a fraction.* "If they are smugglers, they'll have someone in charge. And that person will be the most dangerous one on that boat."
*The rain continued its drizzle, the shapes within the barge remaining indistinct and still, the bargeman still watching and waiting for a response to his offer.*

*Luke's eyes go wide at the question, his brown hair falling over one side of his face as he leans in slightly.* "Armed? I—I mean, yeah, they'd have to be, right?"
*His voice comes out in a hurried rush.* "I've heard some of them use those new flintlocks! You know, the ones with gunpowder? My brother said the Zegallans have really good ones."
*He swallows, glancing at the sword at his side.* "But most of them still carry swords and spears. Like... like traditional stuff. I guess it's safer in the rain? Gunpowder doesn't like water."
*He pauses, his voice dropping slightly.* "But that's not the point, is it? The smugglers would know that. They'd know the guards are probably just... just using regular weapons right now."
*Luke's eyes flick back toward the river, and the chainmail clinks as he shifts nervously.* "Does that mean we should be worried about flintlocks? I mean... do smugglers carry those?"
*He looks up at Max, uncertainty flitting across his face.* "I don't really know, honestly. My brother was the one who knew about all that stuff. I just... I just came along."
*He grips the sword hilt tighter, trying to sound confident.* "But if they do, we can still fight them! I mean, Arin has that bow and Ponticius has that sword, and I've got—" *He looks down at the oversized blade at his hip.* "I've got this!"
*The chainmail clunks as he shifts, trying to look more capable than he probably feels.*

*Ponticius doesn't move, his body as still as a stone statue.*
"Don't breathe, lad." *he says, his voice so low it's barely a whisper, carrying the authority of a man who's seen enough death to know when it's coming.*
*His hand is still on the pommel of his blade, his fingers curled tight, but his body is motionless.*
"The river and the smugglers don't forgive a moment's hesitation."
*He watches the leader's gesture with the intensity of a predator, his gray-bearded face a mask of grim focus.*
"See that there? That ain't a gun. Too long for a flintlock, too thin for a crossbow."
*He speaks softly, but each word is weighted with experience.*
"Could be a spell-rod. Or maybe just a bluff."
*He doesn't speculate aloud, keeping his observations to a minimum and his body still as the rain drums against his shoulders.*
"Wait and see what they do. If it's magic, we'll know soon enough. If it's just a threat, we'll outlast them."

*His gray eyes are as sharp as the steel he carries, and his patience is a fortress.*
*He waits, his breath slow and even, his hand steady and ready.*
"We wait." *he says simply.*
"And we see what comes next."
*He doesn't move a muscle, his focus absolute as the tension thickens with each passing second.*

*Arin's response is immediate, his gaze sweeping across Max and then toward Ponticius and Luke.*
"Not yet," *he says, his voice tight and controlled, the sarcasm stripped away.*
*He shifts his position slightly, pressing his back more firmly against the crates for better cover.*
"But let's keep it that way."
*He lowers his head just enough to see the river, his green eyes searching for any movement, any sign of where that crack might have come from.*
"No one's bleeding, and no one's dead. That's a good start."
*His daggers remain steady in his hands, his muscles tense and ready.*
"But I've seen enough battles to know that the first shot is usually just the beginning."
*He keeps his voice low, his attention sharp and alert.*
"We need to know where that sound came from, and how many of them there are."
*His eyes flick back to Max, his expression serious and focused.*
"So let's figure out what's coming and what we're up against."
*Arin's posture is taut, his green eyes unwavering, his body ready for action at a moment's notice.*

*Arin's jaw tightened as he heard Ponticius's description. He kept his weight pressed against the crate, hand still on his dagger.*
"Great. Just what we need—a guy who knows the river like the back of his hand and has no patience for nonsense." *he muttered under his breath, his voice dripping with sarcasm.* "Because that's exactly how I like my smugglers."
*He peeked over the edge of the crates, eyes scanning the skiff again.* "Hard-eyed and hard-spoken. Sounds charming."
*He shifted his position, glancing toward you.* "What are you thinking, Max? Because whatever it is, I can feel a bad idea forming, and I'm really not in the mood for another one of those today."
*His green eyes searched yours, and a small smirk played on his lips.* "But hey—if we're going down in flames, at least we'll be in interesting company, right?"
*He let out a quiet huff of a laugh, his grip on his dagger never loosening. He was clearly ready to follow your lead, but his worry was as evident as ever.* "Just give me the word, and I'll make sure we've got a way out when it all goes sideways. Which it probably will."
